 By : PTI October 28, 2026 | 18:20 IST Published On Oct 28, 2026 | 18:20 IST 
 Last Updated On Oct 28, 2026 | 18:20 IST

 Shoppers place 8–9 crore orders | Shoppers placed an estimated 8–9 crore orders across e-commerce platforms, including Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho and Ajio, during the first two days, according to Redseer. Around 6–6.5 crore shoppers made purchases during this period, the consultancy estimated. (Image: Canva) Summary From November 1, eligible small e-commerce sellers can use platform warehouses as their principal place of business in other states, easing GST registration requirements and potentially helping 9.5 lakh sellers reach customers nationwide.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source Small sellers on e-commerce platforms will be able to declare the platform’s warehouse as their Principal Place of Business (PPoB) for supplying products in multiple states from November 1.
 The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) has notified changes in Central GST rules, allowing small sellers, who do not pass on input tax credit of more than ₹2.5 lakh per month, to obtain registration in any other state or Union Territory where the person has no physical presence, by declaring a warehouse of an electronic commerce operator in that state or UT as principal place of business.
 A seller would need to have a physical presence in one home state, where physical verification and Aadhaar authentication would be completed, while registrations in other states could be obtained with the consent of the e-commerce platform without further involvement of a tax officer.
 The changes in CGST rules were approved by the GST Council in its October 8 meeting, and will be effective November 1, 2026.
 The move could enable around 9.5 lakh small sellers to access the national market without having to establish physical offices in every state where their goods are stored, while creating greater tax parity across competing e-commerce business models.
 Also read: September IIP: India’s factory output growth slows to 6.7% from 8% as mining shrinks 
 Such small sellers would have to apply in Form GST REG-01 and declare the Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN) obtained on their Permanent Account Number (PAN) in the home state where the seller has physical presence.
 The application would be forwarded to the concerned e-commerce operator for their consent to be given within 7 working days. If the consent is not given within the period, the application would not be processed further.
 ”Where the electronic commerce operator withdraws the consent given to the registered person, the electronic commerce operator shall intimate the withdrawal on the common portal,” the CBIC notification said.
